title: Beginner's Guide: How To Swing Dance (No Experience Needed)

method.teacher_system: The teacher breaks down the swing dance into small, manageable steps, starting with side-to-side movement. He then introduces a rock step and combines these elements into a basic rhythm. Finally, he adds counts and speeds up the tempo to help learners practice.
method.signature: He explicitly frames the lesson as 'social dancing' rather than 'technique', focusing on the ability to move to music in a social setting rather than perfect form.

practices.what: The teacher breaks the dance down into simple side-to-side steps.
The teacher introduces counting to the side-to-side steps.
The teacher introduces the rock step as a separate, backward movement.
The teacher combines the side-to-side steps with the rock step.
The teacher adds specific counts to the combined steps.
The teacher increases the speed of the counts to practice the steps at a faster tempo.

adaptations.difficulty: The learner may be unsure about whether to put their heel back during the rock step.
adaptations.adjustment: The teacher clarifies that it does not matter, focusing on the act of rocking instead.

beliefs.belief: The goal is to learn how to dance socially, not to master complex technique.
If you can do these simple steps, you can dance.
The focus should be on moving in a social setting, not on perfect technique.

feelings.response: The teacher encourages the learner to imagine being in a social situation where everyone is dancing and having fun.

method.limits: The video does not show how to transition between different dance partners or how to handle more complex music rhythms.
